tema: How the Old Testament was Written
palavras: how the old testament was written
resposta: The Old Testament, the Hebrew Bible, was written, compiled, and edited over a period of nearly a thousand years, from about 1000 to 150 B.C.E., by many hands. Tradition ascribes the Torah to Moses, but historical research sees in it various sources and layers of editing.
aprofundar: In the 19th century, Julius Wellhausen formulated the documentary hypothesis: four sources, called J, E, D and P, combined over time. Many scholars today prefer patterns of fragments and supplements, but almost all agree that the Torah took its final form around the time of the Babylonian exile and later, in the sixth and fifth centuries before Christ. The book of Daniel, for example, is generally dated about 164 B.C.E. Practical: Read Genesis one and Genesis two next, and notice that they are two different accounts of creation.
camada3: To contemplate: a people wrote down, over the centuries, their quest for God, with doubts, wars, poetry and prophecy. Can a human text carry the divine? Many believers say yes, for that very reason. The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.

tema: How the New Testament was Written
palavras: how the new testament was written
resposta: The earliest texts of the New Testament are the letters of Paul, about A.D. 50 to 60. The Gospels came later: Mark about 70 C.E., Matthew and Luke about 80 to 90 C.E., and John about 90 to 110 C.E. They circulated anonymously; the titles according to Matthew, according to Mark, were added in the second century.
aprofundar: Of the thirteen letters attributed to Paul, scholars consider seven to be certainly his: Romans, first and second Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, first Thessalonians, and Philemon. Others, such as the letters to Timothy and Titus, are viewed by most as pseudepigrapha, written later in his name, a common practice in antiquity. Practical: Read the entire Gospel of Mark, the oldest, at once.
camada3: For contemplation: Some forty years of oral memory elapsed between the life of Jesus and the early Gospels. What do you keep from someone when all you have left are the memories of those who loved you? The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.

tema: Choosing the Books of the Bible
palavras: how did they choose the books
the apocryphal books of the old testament
choosing the books of the bible
resposta: No one picked everything at once. Around 140 C.E., Marcion proposed a list of his own, with only Luke and ten of Paul's letters, and this forced a reaction. About 180 C.E., Irenaeus defended the four Gospels. In 367, Athanasius of Alexandria listed in an Easter letter the twenty-seven books of the present New Testament. Regional councils in Rome in 382, Hippo in 393, and Carthage in 397 confirmed similar lists.
aprofundar: The list was not definitively fixed for Catholics until the Council of Trent on April 8, 1546, in response to the Reformation. Luther, in his 1534 Bible, singled out the deuterocanonical books, such as Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus, Baruch, and the Maccabees, as good to read but not equal to Scripture. That is why the Catholic Bible has seventy-three books and the evangelical sixty-six. Luther even called the letter of James the straw epistle in 1522.
camada3: To contemplate: human communities, in centuries of debate, have decided what is sacred to them. If the list has changed with the times and the church, where does the ultimate authority lie, on the paper or in the conscience that reads it? The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.

resposta: Constantine legalized Christianity with the Edict of Milan in 313 but did not make it the official religion; this came with Theodosius in the Edict of Thessalonica in 380. He convened the Council of Nicaea in 325, which did NOT choose the books of the Bible; that is the myth popularized by the 2003 book The Da Vinci Code.
aprofundar: Less well-known facts: His coins bore the Unconquered Sun until about 325; in 321 he decreed the day of the Sun, Sunday, as a day of rest; in 326 he had his own son, Crispus, executed, and his wife Fausta died the same year in suspicious circumstances; about 331 he commissioned Eusebius of Caesarea to send fifty copies of the Scriptures to the churches of Constantinople; and he was baptized on his deathbed in 337 by Eusebius of Nicomedia, an Arian bishop.
camada3: To contemplate: the emperor united the cross to the power of Rome. The faith of the persecuted became the faith of the empire. What do you gain and what do you lose when the sacred marries the powerful? The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.

resposta: The Council of Nicaea, in 325, gathered at least two hundred bishops, tradition says three hundred and eighteen, summoned by Constantine. He did NOT choose the books of the Bible. It dealt with three topics: the dispute with the priest Arius, who said that the Son was created and not eternal like the Father; the date of Easter; and norms for the clergy.
aprofundar: The council decided that the Son is homoousios, of the same substance as the Father, and approved the first Nicene Creed. Arius was exiled. Another common myth: That at Nicaea it was voted on whether Jesus was divine; the discussion was not whether he was divine but how. The Arian dispute continued for decades, and Constantine himself later favored Arian bishops.
camada3: To contemplate: one Greek word divided the empire. How many religious quarrels are over words, while love, which they all preach, takes a back seat? The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.

tema: The Lost Gospels and Nag Hammadi
palavras: the lost gospels and nag hammadi
resposta: In December 1945, near Nag Hammadi, Egypt, peasants found a jar with twelve papyrus codices and part of a thirteenth one, with fifty-two Coptic texts, copied in the fourth century. Among them is the complete Gospel of Thomas, with one hundred and fourteen sayings of Jesus.
aprofundar: Other non-canon texts have also appeared: the Gospel of Mary, in a codex purchased in 1896, and the Gospel of Judas, from the Tchacos Codex, published by National Geographic in April 2006, in which Judas appears as the disciple who understood Jesus. Many of these texts are Gnostic and post-canon gospels, but they show how diverse early Christianity was. In the seventy words of Thomas, if you bring to light what is in you, it will save you.
camada3: For contemplation: texts were hidden in a jar to escape destruction. What would you hide so that the truth would survive? The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.

resposta: The Dead Sea Scrolls were found beginning in late 1946 and 1947 by a Bedouin shepherd in the caves of Qumran, and by 1956 the remains of some nine hundred and eighty-one manuscripts, from eleven caves, written between the third century B.C. and the first century A.D., had emerged.
aprofundar: They contain the oldest known manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible, such as the Great Scroll of Isaiah, which is nearly complete and about a thousand years older than the manuscripts used up to that time. They show that the text was well preserved in many books, but also that different versions circulated. Many associate them with the Essenes, but this is debatable.
camada3: For contemplation: truth sometimes sits 2,000 years in a cave waiting to be found. The honesty of the manuscripts is twofold: preservation and variation. Can you accept both? The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.

palavras: the bible has been tampered with
resposta: There are about five thousand eight hundred Greek manuscripts of the New Testament, and none of them are the original. They have many variations, mostly minor, in spelling and word order. But some are large: the episode of the adulterous woman, at John 7:53 to 8:11, and the long ending of Mark, 16:9 to 20, are not in the oldest manuscripts.
aprofundar: The Joanine Comma at 1 John 5:7, the phrase about the three witnesses in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, does not appear in ancient Greek manuscripts; Erasmus included it in the third edition of his Greek New Testament in 1522, and it entered many Bibles. Scholar Bart Ehrman popularized this in his book What Did Jesus Say? Misquoting Jesus, from 2005. Modern Bibles often mark these passages with footnotes.
camada3: For contemplation: copyists, out of care or conviction, changed words. That doesn't erase the teaching of love, but it does call for humility from those who say every comma is untouchable. Read the footnotes in your Bible - the truth is usually there. The spiritual value remains; no institution is owned by God.
